hints.title: Write the component terms
hints.body: Let the ratios of T and U be R and r. Their second terms add to 4R+4r=3; their third terms add to 4R2+4r2=54.
hints.recap: GP term formulas can give symmetric equations for two unknown ratios.
hints.pitfall: The combined series need not itself be geometric.

recall.reminder: GP term formulas can give symmetric equations for two unknown ratios.

hints.title: Recover the product from the square
hints.body: You know R+r=34 and R2+r2=516. Use (R+r)2=R2+r2+2Rr to find Rr.
hints.recap: The square of a sum links a root sum to its product.
hints.pitfall: Remember the factor 2 on the cross term.
hints.pause: Build a monic quadratic whose roots are R and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow></math>.

recall.reminder: The square of a sum links a root sum to its product.

hints.title: Recover the component ratios
hints.body: Use the sum and product to solve for the two ratios. Check convergence separately for each component before adding its sum to infinity.
hints.recap: For an infinite geometric series, first check that the absolute value of the common ratio is below one.
hints.pitfall: The first term and ratio in each sum must come from the same component series.
hints.pause: Solve your quadratic for the ratios, then calculate and add the component sums.

recall.reminder: For an infinite geometric series, first check that the absolute value of the common ratio is below one.

solution:
Let R and r be the two ratios. The supplied terms give R+r=34 and R2+r2=516. Squaring the sum yields 916=516+2Rr, so Rr=18.

Thus R and r are roots of t2−(34)t+18=0, equivalently (2t−1)(4t−1)=0. They are 12 and 14 in either order, so both component series converge.

The total sum is 41−12+41−14=8+163=403, option D. Interchanging the two ratios changes neither this sum nor the given combined terms.
knowledgePattern: Recover two geometric ratios from sum and sum of squares
